title: Terrarium world config
description: Everything needed to start a run: the world seed (physical state plus the records it begins with), seats, framing and parameters. Institutions, laws, procedures and ownership are CONTENT: entities, accounts, records and seats in this config (D23). An empty world is valid. Measurement is deliberately absent. Authored as YAML or JSON; the orchestrator converts it to canonical JSON, and that exact JSON is embedded in the log header.

seed.description: Seed for the kernel's single source of randomness (keyed streams, D7).

max_created_entities.description: Researcher's experimental control on how many entities seats may declare in a run.

orchestration.description: Recorded so the run is fully described; enforced by the orchestrator, not the kernel.

confirm.description: When a language seat sees and confirms what its plain-language request will do before it takes effect (docs/design/translator-and-resolver.md §10). Default 'always'. 'consequential': everything except plain messages. 'never': immersion, audited offline.

category.description: A label for people and laws to refer to (residential, commercial, green...). The kernel attaches no meaning to it.

capacity.description: Physical capacity by slot kind, e.g. {"dwelling": 12} or {"workplace": 8}.

boundary.description: The single entity of kind 'boundary': the world's outside. Its account (custodian: itself) may go negative; total money including it is constant for the whole run. Money enters the world only when the outside world's own seat pays from that account (D31): exports bought, visitors' spending, grants. How much is researcher-set world content.

parcels.description: Land is finite: this is all of it. Axis-aligned, non-overlapping rectangles on an integer grid.

custodian.description: The entity that physically holds the money: a bank, or the holder itself (cash-like).

balance.description: Opening balance; >= 0 except for the boundary's account.

structures.description: Structures standing at t=0 (complete). Ownership, if any, is a record.

occupancy.description: Who physically occupies what at t=0.

records.description: The records the world begins with: its laws, procedures and organisation structures; who owns what; agreements in force; debts outstanding. Usually authored 'genesis'.

kind.description: A label. Two are reserved and physical: 'person' (a body: exists, is somewhere, can't be created by a block) and 'boundary' (the world's edge; exactly one). Everything else (government, council, bank, firm, trust, union...) is the world's vocabulary.

Seat.description: A role or person that acts in the world: a mayor, a bank's payment system, a planning officer, a citizen. The kernel uses only 'entity' (whose hands this seat is, which determines what it can physically do, e.g. move money in that entity's custody) and 'channels' (what it can perceive). Every seat can always opt out of the study (VISION §15; D38); 'on_opt_out' says what happens to it afterwards.

entity.description: The entity this seat acts as: a person's own seat, or an organisation's (the city's finance officer is a seat of 'city'). Authority within the organisation is a matter of its records (roles, procedures), not of the kernel.

role.description: Optional label of the role this seat fills in its organisation's records (e.g. 'mayor', 'finance_officer'). Informational for the kernel.

on_opt_out.description: What happens to the seat if its controller opts out of the study: 'vacant' (default; the seat never acts again, and in the world the person simply stops acting) or a code stand-in that takes over. Recorded, never judged.

Channel.description: A perception channel. Every seat also always receives its inbox and the outcomes of its own acts. Records are only ever shown if their visibility allows the seat's entity to see them.

title.description: What the seat's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

kind.description: Balances and new transactions of accounts the seat's entity holds or has custody of.

title.description: What the seat's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

match.description: Which records this channel shows (all conditions must hold; omitted means any).

involving.description: Records naming any of these entities (as holder, counterparty, party, addressee, author's entity or speaks_for), or referring to a record that does (a signature on their agreement, a withdrawal of their statement, a vote on their ballot; one hop). 'self' means the seat's own entity.

new_only.description: Show only records made since the seat's previous observation.

title.description: What the seat's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

kind.description: Physical state of parcels in an area: structures, construction under way, occupancy. How inspectors see.

every.description: How often the view refreshes. Between refreshes the seat sees the state as of the last refresh. Coverage and frequency are experimental variables.

title.description: What the seat's reports call this channel (e.g. 'Treasury', 'Council business'). Presentation only; the kernel ignores it.

kind.description: Who exists: entities and seats (names, kinds, titles).

Controller.description: Who fills the seat. Opaque to the kernel. Code controllers name a behaviour module (content: documented and cited in docs/behaviour/).

Framing.description: What the seat is told about its situation (VISION §9.3, §15.1). The reason is mandatory: deception is a method, not a default.

debrief_text.description: What the seat is told at the end of the run, if debrief is set. Default: the orchestrator's (docs/design/m2-llm-seats.md), which says what the run was, discloses any framing and asks for the seat's reaction.
